MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 28, 2020

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Goodell at 5:01 p.m., on January 28, 2020, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 23, 2020, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley (arrived at 5:05 p.m.)
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Goodell recessed the meeting. The City Council reconvened at
6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Goodell

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize the 2019 Employees of the Year

City Council Minutes  1  January 28, 2020
   Mayor Goodell presented plaques to (1) Animal Services Volunteer Coordinator, Giselle
  Leal-Pelayo, City of Mission Viejo Employee of the Year; (2) Fire Captain Chuck Hawkins,
  Orange County Fire Authority Employee of the Year; and (3) Deputy Wayne Dixon, Orange
  County Sheriff’s Department Employee of the Year.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve
the Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of January 14, 2020, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated January 10, 2020 in the Amount of $1,407,424.42

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Zone Change ZC2019-22, Being a Petition Submitted by Confluent Development, to
  Place a Senior Housing Overlay Zone on 2.92 Acres of Property Located at 28570
  Marguerite Parkway, in the CH (Commercial Highway) Zone, Further Described as
  Assessor Parcel Number 740-012-21

  Adopted Ordinance 20-335 Approving Zone Change Zc2019-22, Being a Petition Submitted
  by Confluent Development, to Place a Senior Housing Overlay Zone on 2.92 Acres of
  Property Located at 28570 Marguerite Parkway, in the CH (Commercial Highway) Zone,
  Further Described as Assessor Parcel Number 740-012-2.

4.  Professional Services Agreement for Solid Waste and Recycling Consulting Services -
  Contract Change Order 1

  Authorized the approval of Contract Change Order 1 for Solid Waste and Recycling
  Consulting Services in the amount of $34,502 to Sloan Vasquez McAfee.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

5.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Sachs.

6.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report
City Council Minutes  2  January 28, 2020
   Received report from Council Member Bucknum.

7.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Received report from Council Member Bucknum.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

8.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum stated that she attended the Chamber of Commerce Mixer that was
held at the Leonard Cancer Institute next to Mission Hospital. She indicated that currently the
Institute will take patients that need medical scans since they are not busy as of yet.

Council Member Raths

9.  Consideration of a Request to Amend the City Council’s Temporary Sign Policy 0600-
  06

  Council Member Raths presented his Council Report.

  Tom Moore, M.V.: Complained about the political signs at the intersections and suggested
  15 days prior to the election was sufficient amount of time that signs be displayed.

  City staff answered Council Member’s questions.

  Council Member Sachs asked to bifurcate the motion.

  Motion made by Council Member Raths, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to
  adopt Resolution 20-02 Amending Criteria for Placement of Temporary Signs in the Public
  Right-Of-Way at Arterial Intersections for 30 Days Prior to the Distribution of the Ballots
  for any Government Agency Election and Amending City Council Policy 0600-6.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Raths to enforce
  the sign policy and keep the $240 Sign Deposit.

City Council Minutes  3  January 28, 2020
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs expressed his appreciation of City Staff that on April 21st Holocaust
Remembrance Day the City will have displays at both the Norman P. Murry Center and the Potocki
Center. He highlighted some of the atrocities that occurred during the Holocaust and
recommended a book entitled “ 999: The Extraordinary Young Women of the First Official Jewish
Transport to Auschwitz”. Reiterated that he is very proud of the City for standing up and putting
on this exhibition and encouraged residents to attend.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that she attended a ribbon cutting ceremony for the new UFC
Gym located in Olympiad Plaza where they were treated to a demonstration. She stated that she
also attended the Chamber Mixer at the Leonard Cancer Institute along with Council Member
Bucknum, Mayor Goodell and Council Member Raths. She expressed that this Institute is a state-
of-the-art facility and will be an asset to Mission Viejo. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley reported that
she also attended the ribbon cutting ceremony for the new City of Hope facility in Newport
Beach and the State of the County where Lisa Bartlett gave an update on the County. Lastly, she
attended the South Orange County Economic Coalition where a panel gave a presentation on
health care that was very informational.

Mayor Goodell

10. Consideration of Request to Support the "Reducing Crime and Keeping California
  Safe Act of 2020"

  Mayor Goodell presented his City Council Report.

  Motion made by Mayor Goodell, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley to adopt Resolution
  20-03 Supporting the Reducing Crime and Keeping California Safe Act of 2020.

Mayor Goodell announced that he attended the Capo Innovation Showcase at Capo Valley High
School. Commended all the students that participated and stated that he had a really nice time.
Lastly, he mentioned that the Capistrano Valley High School Robot Team is one of the best in the
State and is ranked in the top 50 in the United States.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:48 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Goodell adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, February 11, 2020, at 5:00 p.m.

City Council Minutes  4  January 28, 2020
 ______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 11, 2020

City Council Minutes  5  January 28, 2020
